title: Land Plot Splitting and Merging Conditions 2026 under Land Law 2024
desc: Conditions for splitting or merging land plots under Article 220 of the 2024 Land Law: certificate, valid term, no dispute, access, provincial minimum area.
summary: General and specific conditions for splitting and merging land plots under Article 220 of the 2024 Land Law, provincially set minimum areas, and points to note when dividing land for children or selling part of a plot.
body: p

Dividing land for your children, selling off part of a plot, or merging two adjoining plots to build a larger house all require a plot-splitting or plot-merging procedure. The nationwide general conditions are in Article 220 of the 2024 Land Law; specific areas and dimensions are set by each province.
h2
1. General conditions for both splitting and merging
p
Under Clause 1, Article 220, the land plot must:
ol
Have been issued a certificate (any of the types of red book or pink book (sổ đỏ, sổ hồng) issued under the laws of different periods).
Still be within its land use term.

Not be in dispute, not be distrained to secure judgment enforcement, and not be subject to a provisional urgent measure. If part of the plot is disputed but the extent and boundary of the disputed part can be determined, the remaining part may still be split or merged.
Ensure access, connection to the existing public road, and reasonable water supply, drainage and other necessary needs.
p

If the landholder sets aside part of a residential plot (or a plot with residential and other land) as an access path when splitting or merging, no change of land use purpose is required for that access path.
h2
2. Specific conditions for splitting
ul

The plots resulting from the split must meet the minimum area for the type of land in use as prescribed by the provincial People's Committee. A split-off plot smaller than the minimum must be merged at the same time with an adjoining plot (Point a, Clause 2).

Changing the purpose of part of a plot requires splitting, and the resulting plot must meet the minimum area for the type of land after the change of purpose. For a plot with residential and other land, splitting is not compulsory when changing the purpose of part of it, unless the landholder wishes to (Point b, Clause 2).
Where land is divided under a court judgment or decision that does not satisfy the splitting conditions, area or dimensions, the plot is not split (Point c, Clause 2).
h2
3. Specific conditions for merging
ul

The plots must have the same use purpose and the same term and the same form of land rent payment, except for merging plots containing residential and other land with each other or with a residential plot (Point a, Clause 3).

Where the purpose, term or form of rent payment differs, the procedures to change the purpose, adjust the term and change the form of rent payment must be carried out at the same time to make them uniform (Point b, Clause 3).
h2
4. Where to find the minimum area for splitting
p

Under Clause 4, Article 220, the provincial People's Committee, based on the law, related regulations and local customs and practices, sets the specific conditions and minimum areas for splitting and merging for each type of land. Each province sets a different level, so landholders should look up the decision of the provincial People's Committee where the land is located or ask the land registration office.
h2
5. Points to note when dividing or selling part of a plot
ul
A plot split off for sale must meet the transfer conditions under Article 45 of the Land Law, and the contract must be notarised or certified; see Notarising a house and land sale contract in 2026.
Splitting or merging changes boundaries and area, so a change registration is required (Point d, Clause 1, Article 133).
A small or oddly shaped plot after splitting may be hard to get a building permit for or may fail the setback requirement; ask a design firm before dividing the land.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The 2024 Land Law is partly expired; no amendment to Article 220 has been found in our library. The dossier, order of procedure and competent authority for splitting and merging follow the decree on land registration and the provincial People's Committee's rules after the 2-level government reorganisation in 2025 - ask the land registration office where the land is located.
